result.topic_en: Tables of geometric progressions of each residue b coprime to the divisor d (d = 7, 8, 9, 10, 11) and their residues mod d, showing the exponent n at which the power first leaves remainder 1, compared with μ (the count of residues prime to d).

methods.what: Computing the multiplicative order n of b modulo d by listing residues of successive powers until 1 recurs, for d=7
methods.quote: Si divisor $d=7$, erit $\mu=6$ totidemque habentur casus

methods.what: Modulo 8 every unit has order dividing 2 (no primitive root): orders compared to μ=φ(8)=4
methods.quote: nullo ergo casu erit $n=\mu$, sed tribus $n=\frac{1}{2}\mu$, et uno casu $n=\frac{1}{4}\mu$.

methods.what: Orders of units modulo 9 (φ(9)=6; 2 and 5 have order 6)
methods.quote: Si divisor sit $d=9$, erit $\mu=6$ totidemque casus

methods.what: Orders of units modulo 10 (φ(10)=4; 3 and 7 have order 4)
Orders of units modulo 11 (φ(11)=10; 2 has order 10)

items.quote: nullo ergo casu erit $n=\mu$, sed tribus $n=\frac{1}{2}\mu$, et uno casu $n=\frac{1}{4}\mu$.
items.english: Therefore in no case will n = μ, but in three cases n = ½μ, and in one case n = ¼μ.
